What is Camelot?

Why does Camelot stay memorable?

It stays memorable because the central image is easy to picture and difficult to exhaust. Readers can approach it through history, belief, science, literature, or place memory without losing the main shape.

Is every version treated as literal proof?

No. The article treats the material as a source-aware record. It allows tradition and wonder to remain visible, but it does not turn uncertainty into proof or flatten all sources into one claim.

How is the article organized?

The article uses fewer, stronger sections and longer connected paragraphs. It follows the subject through identity, setting, source limits, and modern meaning so the page reads like a continuous explanation instead of a list.

How should readers use the sources?

Readers should treat the sources as context layers. Some explain tradition, some explain history or natural process, and some show later reception. The strongest reading keeps those layers distinct.
